objectives: Explain what we ask for in 1:6
Connect the surah to daily prayer
records.environment: A symbolic path (Al-Fatihah has no story): a gate of praise hung with flowers (1:2), a garden of mercy where dry beds bloom when watered (1:3, with 30:50), a terrace facing a wide dawn horizon (1:4; nothing of the Day is pictured) and a fork where one bright road runs straight (1:6).

themes: Adam and the knowledge of names

passages.title: Ibrahim and Ismail raise the House
The town and the hundred years

objectives: Name the main stories in Al-Baqarah
Explain the seed example of charity
Understand that knowledge comes from Allah
records.environment: A green valley of guidance: an orchard where hidden things are found by name (2:31), a meadow of cows (2:67), great foundation stones (2:127), a river to cross (2:249) and a field where one seed grows seven spikes (2:261).

themes: The family of Imran and Maryam
objectives: Retell Maryam's provision in the prayer chamber
Explain holding firmly to the rope of Allah
Practise reflecting on night and day
records.environment: A sanctuary in morning light: a small chamber with fruit in a lit niche, no one shown (3:37), a courtyard of pillars bound by one rope (3:103), a rooftop where a sundial marks the turning of night and day (3:190) and a distant gateway (3:96).

objectives: Name people the Quran asks us to be kind to
records.environment: A village of trusts and justice: a square with one fountain from which channels run (4:1), houses waiting for what was lent to come back (4:58), a lane of neighbours (4:36) and tall scales (4:135).

objectives: Retell the lesson of the crow
Understand that saving one life is precious
records.environment: A hall of promises (5:1), an olive grove where a crow scratches the ground (5:31), one lantern that lights a whole hall (5:32) and a long table under an arch, spread and empty (5:114).

passages.title: Ibrahim and the star, moon and sun

objectives: Explain why things that set are not worthy of worship
Name signs of Allah in plants
records.environment: A night of signs turning to dawn: a ridge where a bright star sets (6:76), a plain where the moon rises (6:77), an overlook at sunrise (6:78), a valley where seeds split and sprout (6:95) and date palms with low clusters (6:99).

The heights: a garden with one tree (7:19), timbers of a ship on a hill (7:64), wide windy plains (7:65), homes carved in cliffs (7:74), a market where weights must be fair (7:85) and a calm shore (7:138).

passages.title: Rain before the day of Badr

objectives: Know that Allah's help comes with patience
records.environment: A field where rain falls and the sand grows firm (8:11), a circle of stones that glows (8:2) and a green hill of peace (8:61).

passages.title: The three who were left behind

records.environment: A small empty cave in the hills (9:40), a simple mosque on firm foundations (9:108-109) and a circle of stones for learning (9:122).

passages.title: Musa and Pharaoh at the sea

objectives: Explain moon phases as a sign
Know that the people of Yunus believed
records.environment: A terrace of the moon's phases for counting the months (10:5), a ship at sea (10:22), a garden in the rain (10:24) and a doorway to Yunus's story (10:98).

objectives: Name the messengers in Surah Hud
records.environment: The ark coast, following 11:36-48: a shipyard where the ark's last planks are fitted (11:37), the loading ground where animals come aboard two by two and the weather turns (11:40), a stormy bay with waves like mountains (11:42), the green slopes where the ark rests (11:44), and an empty tent with a roasted calf for guests (11:69). Nuh, his family and the guests are never shown; the animal kinds are the artist's choice.

objectives: Explain how planning helped during hardship
records.environment: Seven connected places follow the surah in order: the night of eleven stars, the well, the caravan road, a house in Egypt, the prison, the storehouses and the reunion hall.

objectives: Explain the example of water and foam
records.environment: The valley of thunder: rivers running between mountains (13:3), neighbouring plots growing different fruits from one water (13:4), a ridge and a rocky hall under thunder clouds (13:12-13) and a pool where foam drifts away (13:17).

objectives: Know Ibrahim prayed for his family
records.environment: A good tree with deep roots and high branches (14:24), an uprooted tree lying loose (14:26), a dry valley (14:37) and a river with sailing boats (14:32).

themes: Signs in the sky and earth
objectives: Learn about the people of al-Hijr
records.environment: A rocky tract under the stars: constellations (15:16), firm mountains (15:19), winds carrying pollen to flowers (15:22) and empty homes carved in the cliffs (15:82).

objectives: Describe what the Quran says about bees
records.environment: A valley of blessings: rounded cliffs and a tree with bees' homes and wooden hives (16:68), honey jars in different colours (16:69), a pasture with a fold and a barn (16:5-6, 16:66), a lagoon with a boat and pearl shells (16:14) and birds held up in the sky (16:79). No person is shown.

objectives: Know how to speak to parents
records.environment: A path of lamps through the night (17:1: nothing of the journey is depicted), two signs, the sun and the moon (17:12), a family courtyard (17:23) and a market with honest scales (17:35).
Four connected adventures: the cave of the young believers, the two gardens, the meeting of the two seas, and the iron barrier.

objectives: Retell Maryam's account from the ayahs
records.environment: A quiet chamber (19:11), a tall palm in a remote place (19:23) with a stream below it (19:24) and ripe dates (19:25), and a mountain slope (19:52). No one is shown.

passages.title: The dry path in the sea
Adam and the lesson of guidance

objectives: Explain why the calf was wrong to worship
records.environment: A fire glowing far across a dark valley (20:10), a pair of sandals left at the valley's edge (20:12, an adaptation), a chest in the reeds (20:39), a dry path between walls of water (20:77) and an empty camp (20:88). Musa and every person are never shown; no idol is pictured.

objectives: Explain the shared message of all prophets
records.environment: Rooms of signs: a spring (21:30), an empty ring of stones where the fire was made cool (21:69; no fire or person is shown), mountains with birds (21:79), a sail full of wind (21:81) and a dark sea at night (21:87).

themes: Signs of resurrection in the earth
objectives: Explain who first proclaimed Hajj in the surah
records.environment: Roads from far mountain passes with camels (22:27), simple foundations (22:26), dry fields that turn green as rain falls (22:63) and a slope where plants stir (22:5).

objectives: List the qualities of believers in 23:1-11
records.environment: Terraces of the successful believers: a quiet stepped terrace (23:2-3), rain held in great basins (23:18), palms and vines (23:19), a great olive tree (23:20) and an empty shipyard (23:27).

Doors that open after greeting (24:27), a glass lamp in a niche like a bright star (24:35), a blessed olive grove (24:35), a mirage plain (24:39), a dark sea (24:40) and birds with spread wings (24:41).

themes: Qualities of the servants of Allah
records.environment: A sundial field where shadows move with the sun (25:45), winds driving clouds (25:48), two waters side by side with a barrier (25:53), the sun and the moon (25:61) and a gentle path (25:63).

themes: Every messenger called to worship Allah
records.environment: Seven shores: towering walls of water either side of a path (26:63), a meadow of many noble kinds (26:7), rock-cut homes, empty (26:149) and a thicket by a market with scales (26:176-183).

themes: Turning from false worship to Allah
objectives: Retell the ant and the hoopoe
Explain that the Queen turned to Allah
records.environment: A journey with Sulayman's story told from the land around it: the valley of the ants, the hoopoe's flight to Sheba, a throne that appears in a blink, and a palace whose floor looks like water.

objectives: Explain why Qarun's wealth did not help
records.environment: Reeds and calm water (28:7), the well of Madyan with flocks waiting (28:23), a tree's shade (28:24), a fire seen from the road (28:29) and a treasure house sinking into the ground (28:81).
A huge, fine spider's web (29:41), a road through many landscapes (29:20) and an ark resting on a ridge as a sign (29:15).

objectives: Explain why diversity is a sign
Name two signs from the surah
records.environment: A market of many languages (30:22), a harbour with ships on good winds (30:46), clouds that spread and break into rain (30:48) and bare land returning to green (30:50).
A great rock with a tiny seed beside it (31:16), a path for walking gently (31:19) and a shore with trees and a pen (31:27).
A riverbank of clay (32:7), a village with lamps at night (32:16) and dry land receiving water (32:27).

themes: The Prophet as the best example
Good character for men and women
objectives: Explain why the Prophet (peace be upon him) is the best example
records.environment: Wind sweeping through empty tents (33:9) and mountains that stand for the trust (33:72, symbolic).

themes: Craft as a gift from Allah
objectives: Name the gifts of Dawud and Sulayman
records.environment: Hills that echo with praise and birds (34:10), a glowing spring of copper (34:12), great basins (34:13), gardens on both sides of a dam (34:15) and a broken one where the trees fell (34:16).
Mountains streaked white, red and black (35:27), orchards in many colours (35:27) and two seas, fresh and salt, with pearls (35:12).

passages.title: The town and the man who came running

records.environment: Dead earth that bursts with grain (36:33), palms and springs (36:34), the moon's phases (36:39), a laden ship (36:41) and a green tree with a fire (36:80).
A sky adorned with stars (37:6), an open shore (37:145) and a gourd vine over a shady spot (37:146).
Hills that echo at sunrise (38:18), birds gathering (38:19) and a cool spring (38:42).
Rain running underground into springs (39:21), crops that grow, turn yellow and dry (39:21) and a soft light on the horizon (39:73; nothing of Paradise is pictured).
A brick tower that stops far short of the sky (40:36-37) and a simple house (40:28). No one is shown.

themes: Signs in the horizons and in ourselves
objectives: Explain rain as a sign of life
records.environment: A sky of drifting mist (41:11), a still dry plain (41:39) that stirs and sprouts when rain falls (41:39).
A harbour of ships like mountains (42:32), ships lying still when the wind stops (42:33) and a circle of seats for deciding together (42:38).
Roads across the earth (43:10), rain in measure reviving dead land (43:11), and ships and animals to ride (43:12).

themes: The Quran revealed on a blessed night
records.environment: A calm blessed night (44:3), a sea lying still (44:24) and gardens and springs left behind (44:25).
Ships sailing (45:12) and a wide view of sky and land, with birds and grazing animals (45:13).
Wind-curved dunes (46:21), a cloud approaching the valleys (46:24) and a quiet night valley with standing stones (46:29; nothing unseen is shown).

themes: The reward described in the Quran
objectives: Explain helping Allah's cause by good deeds
records.environment: A reading stand with the ayah that describes rivers (47:15; the rivers themselves are not pictured), a quiet garden and stepping stones for steady feet (47:7).
A single tree on a plain, no one shown (48:18), and a shoot growing strong on its stalk (48:29).

themes: Manners with the Prophet (peace be upon him)
records.environment: A friendly village where each street teaches a manner from the surah: checking news, making peace, no mocking, no nicknames, no spying, no backbiting, and a market square where peoples and tribes meet to know one another.

objectives: Explain that Allah knows our thoughts
records.environment: A sky without rifts (50:6), mountains and beautiful plants (50:7), blessed rain over grain (50:9) and lofty palms with layered fruit (50:10).
Winds scattering dust (51:1), clouds heavy with water (51:2), ships sailing easily (51:3) and a wide sky (51:47).

themes: Patience of the Prophet (peace be upon him)
records.environment: A lone mountain (52:1), an open scroll on a stone (52:3) and a high sky (52:5).

themes: Each person carries their own deeds
records.environment: A star setting (53:1), a valley of sunshine and soft rain, standing for joy and tears (53:43; no faces) and the bright star Sirius (53:49).

themes: The Quran is easy to remember
records.environment: A full moon over the plain (54:1; the splitting itself is not pictured), pouring rain (54:11), springs bursting from the earth (54:12), a vessel of planks being built (54:13) and palms uprooted by the wind (54:20).

A world built as a series of balanced gardens and shores, each closing with the surah's refrain 'So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?', from the sun and moon in precise calculation to the two seas meeting with pearls and coral.

objectives: Explain that the Event is unseen
records.environment: A field where seeds are planted (56:63), rain falling into a well (56:69) and a tree with a fire for travellers (56:72).
A field that grows and turns yellow (57:20), a forge with iron (57:25) and earth returning to life (57:17).
An open hall where room is made for others (58:11), with seats in a circle and houses around.

objectives: Name some of the names in 59:22-24
records.environment: A great mountain, humbled (59:21), and a reading stand with the ayahs of Allah's names (59:22-24; the names are read from the verified text, not drawn in the sky).
A bridge over a stream for fair dealings (60:8) and a garden of hope (60:7).
A wall of tightly joined stones (61:4).
Market stalls shut for the Friday prayer (62:9) and reopened afterwards (62:10).

themes: Spending before it is too late
records.environment: Baskets of harvest to share before the time runs out (63:10).
A path of steps up a slope, where effort counts (64:16).
A spring appearing in a dry place (65:3).
A palace room (66:11) and a quiet sanctuary with fruit in a lit niche (66:12). No one is shown.
A sky without flaw to look at again and again (67:3-4), slopes to walk (67:15) and birds with outspread wings (67:19).
A pen and inkwell (68:1), a garden ready to harvest at dawn (68:17) and a garden that looks reaped (68:20).
A windswept valley (69:6) with hollow palm trunks lying fallen (69:7).
Garden steps rising gently and a quiet place of steady prayer (70:23); nothing unseen is shown.

objectives: Explain the sun and moon in 71:16
records.environment: The promise of 71:10-12 told through the land: three dry fields that turn green when the child brings rain clouds, a riverbed that fills beside fruit trees, two pedestals for the moon as "a [reflected] light" and the sun as "a burning lamp" (71:16), and roads winding through wide hills (71:19-20). Nuh and his people are never shown; the seven heavens are not pictured.

themes: Unseen beings exist but are not shown
records.environment: A still desert under the stars (72:1) and shooting stars across the sky (72:8). Nothing unseen is shown.
A dial of the night hours (73:2-4) and a reading stand for slow, measured recitation (73:4).
Sunrise over a home (74:2) and a washing place with clean cloth (74:4).
A pattern of fingertip whorls in light on a stone (75:4).
An open doorway where food is shared (76:8).
Winds in gusts (77:1), the earth that holds (77:25) and mountains with sweet water (77:27).

A walk through the signs of 78:6-16: a soft meadow with a resting bench (78:6), mountains standing like stakes (78:7), a starry canopy that covers like clothing (78:10), a bright sun disc like a burning lamp (78:13), and gardens of vines grown thickly together (78:16). The Day of 78:17-40 is not pictured. No person is shown.

A high open place under a wide raised sky (79:28), a spring bubbling out of the ground into a green pasture (79:31), and mountains set firmly around the valley (79:32). The story of Musa and Pharaoh (79:15-26) is told only in the reading, not shown, and the Day of 79:34-46 is not pictured. No person is shown.

themes: Humility and caring for every person
records.environment: A walk that follows food from the start: a torrent of water pouring down rocks (80:25), earth split open by sprouts (80:26), rows of grain and grapevines on a trellis (80:27-28), olive and palm trees (80:29), and fruit trees over grass (80:31). The event of 80:1-10 and the Day of 80:33-42 are not pictured. No person is shown.

objectives: Explain that the Day is described in the Quran
records.environment: Late night. Stars run low and slip below the horizon, mirrored in a still pool (81:15-16); a dark grove holds the night as it closes in (81:17); and at the end of the path a dawn glow rises while a soft breeze moves the grass, the dawn as it breathes (81:18). The events of 81:1-14 are not pictured. No person is shown.

A garden of forms that are well made and balanced: a great spiral shell, a symmetrical leaf in stone and an arch balanced on its own stones (82:7). Beside it, a table of fruit and water, gifts that remind us that our Lord is the Generous (82:6). The breaking sky and scattered stars of 82:1-4 are not pictured. No person is shown.

A morning market stall: a pair of honest scales with brass weights (83:3), and sacks of grain beside an empty wooden measure that can be filled right to the brim (83:2). No person is shown, and the Day, the registers and the next life of 83:4-36 are not pictured.

Evening: a band of twilight glow lingers on the horizon (84:16) as night gathers (84:17), and a large full moon rises (84:18). A row of eight stone discs shows the moon's phases, state after state (84:19). The splitting of the sky and the Day (84:1-15) are not pictured. No person is shown.

A night of great bright stars (85:1). Further on, an old, empty trench overgrown with grass, long after the events of 85:4-8: no fire and no people are shown. Last, a reading stand with a closed, covered book for the honoured Quran (85:21). The Preserved Slate (85:22) is not pictured.

A clear night with one star brighter than the rest, its light sharp and piercing (86:3). Further on, a small cloud keeps returning rain onto a patch of ground (86:11), where the earth cracks open and sprouts push through (86:12). No person is shown.

A wide field beside the path: one part fresh green pasture (87:4), and further on the same grass dried to dark stubble (87:5). The field slowly turns from green to dark and grows again, a picture of how short the life of this world is. The Fire of 87:12 is not pictured. No person is shown.

A walk past the four things 88:17-20 asks us to look at: resting camels, a high open lookout for the raised sky, tall mountains standing up from the plain, and a wide flat plain spread out to the horizon. The Day and the Garden described in 88:1-16 are not pictured. No person is shown.

A dawn lookout (89:1). Further on, the weathered ruins of very tall pillars for Iram, who had lofty pillars (89:7), and a valley where doorways are carved into the rock for Thamud (89:9). Both are artistic stand-ins, empty and quiet, not the real places. No person is shown; the punishment of 89:13 and the Day of 89:21-26 are not pictured.

The path forks into two ways (90:10): an easy path that wanders off, and a steep, narrow pass between rocks (90:11). At the top of the pass waits a table set for feeding on a day of hunger (90:14). No person is shown, and the fire of 90:20 is not pictured.

A sundial in a bright square (91:1) and a still round pool beside it, where the moon is seen when it follows the sun (91:2). Further on, an old stone well with an empty drinking trough (91:13) below cliffs with carved doorways, for Thamud (91:11). No person and no she-camel are shown, and the destruction of 91:14 is not pictured.

A courtyard split in two: one half tiled in deep blue with lanterns and night flowers for "the night when it covers" (92:1), the other in warm gold with sunflowers for "the day when it appears" (92:2). Beside it, a table set out for giving (92:5, 92:18). No person is shown. The Fire and the next life are not pictured.

Bright morning light fills a meadow (93:1), while a thick grove nearby keeps the shade of the night (93:2). Further on, a home stands with its door open, a bench and a water jug outside, for kindness to the orphan and the one who asks (93:9-10). No person is shown.

The path climbs a steep, stony stretch, then opens onto an easy, level meadow path (94:5-6). A heavy pack lies set down beside the way, a picture of a burden removed (94:2). Stones block part of the path and can be cleared. No person is shown.

themes: Allah is the most just judge
records.environment: The path runs between a fig orchard and an olive grove (95:1). Far off stands a tall mountain for Mount Sinai (95:2) and a small walled city in a valley for the secure city (95:3). Both are simple stand-ins seen from far away, not their real shapes. No person is shown.

A rocky hill rises over the path with a small cave high on its side. The surah does not describe this place; the cave follows the hadith of the first revelation and is labelled as such. Below, a writing desk holds a reed pen, ink and blank paper (96:4), and a quiet terrace invites prostration (96:19). No person is shown.

A still night. A long low wall holds a thousand tiny lamps, one for each month, for 97:3. Beyond it, a quiet hill faces the east, where the sky slowly brightens toward dawn (97:5). The angels and the Spirit of 97:4 are not pictured; no person is shown.

A calm morning court with a reading stand holding a closed, covered book, for the purified scriptures and correct writings of 98:2-3, and a clear spring beside a prayer terrace for 98:5. No person is shown, and the Fire and the gardens of the next life (98:6-8) are not pictured.

A morning garden where tiny specks of dust drift in shafts of sunlight and rows of very small seedlings grow. They show how small an atom's weight is (99:7-8): even the smallest good is seen. The earthquake of 99:1 and the Day are not pictured. No person is shown.

At dawn, a line of horses gallops across the dunes, panting (100:1, 100:3); sparks fly where their hooves strike the stones (100:2) and clouds of dust rise behind them (100:4). The horses carry no riders; no person is shown.

A night path where moths flutter and scatter around lamps (101:4), and a field of hills with heaps of fluffed wool beside them (101:5). These are only the Quran's comparisons, shown as everyday things: the Day of 101:1-3, the scales and the Fire are not pictured. No person is shown.

Towers of crates, jars and boxes stacked higher and higher beside the path, each trying to outgrow the last (102:1). Further on, a quiet walled graveyard with plain, unmarked stones (102:2). No person is shown. The Day of Judgement and the Fire are not pictured.
A world built inside the flow of time: sand pouring from a vast hourglass across a dune landscape, and four keys that save from loss: faith, good deeds, advising truth and advising patience.
An empty counting room at dusk: a table heaped with coins, an open ledger and an abacus, and locked chests along the wall. No person is shown. The Day of Judgement and the Fire are not pictured.
A dusty road to Makkah where a great army with an elephant comes, birds in flocks gather over the hills, and the army becomes like eaten straw; the House stands untouched.

A desert road with two resting caravans of camels and loads, one with winter wraps and one with summer shades (106:2). A well and baskets of food stand by the road (106:4). The House of 106:3 is seen far off in a valley, simply, without detail. No people are shown.
A small morning street: a home with an open door and a bench (107:2), a table with bread and water (107:3) and a shelf of small things to lend, like a bucket and a pot (107:7). No people are shown.
An orchard with full baskets, a sign of good things given. It is not a picture of al-Kawthar, which is not shown. A small clean terrace for prayer stands at its edge. No person is shown.
A meadow path divides into two paths that run side by side to the horizon and never cross. Paired standing stones mark the repeated ayahs. No people are shown.
Many paths from every direction meet at an open gate, marked with lanterns that come on one by one. Beyond it is a quiet terrace for praise. No people are shown: the paths stand for the multitudes.
A dusk road past an abandoned heap of chests and coins that does no good to anyone, and a bundle of firewood tied with a twisted rope. No person is shown, and the Fire of 111:3 is not pictured.
A quiet courtyard of geometric tiles, a shaded shelter and an open terrace facing an empty sky, where the four ayahs are read. No image, figure or symbol stands for Allah.
A ridge facing the eastern horizon as daybreak comes, and a low hollow below it where the evening shadow settles. Lanterns light the hollow. No person, magic or envier is shown.
A lane of tall reeds that rustle and whisper in the wind, leading to a small lit stone shelter. The whisper is only the sound of reeds; no whisperer, jinn or person is shown.
